mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.5% (current value: 2.4) signals monetary easing, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in <60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% over a 3-year rolling window, or returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and increase in consumer demand (FEDFUNDS < 2.5% and GDPC1 > 18,000) creates a dual easing environment, amplifying equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Over the next 20 days, S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS declining and GDPC1 increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in consumer demand (GDPC1 above 18,000) signals robust economic activity, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 remains above 18,000 but S&P 500 returns over 20 days are not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) and strong consumer demand (GDPC1) create a dual positive momentum, amplifying market confidence and driving S&P 500 returns upwards over 20 days.
failure_condition: Either GDPC1 or PAYEMS moves against their expected directions (GDPC1 above 18k and PAYEMS below 150k), yet returns remain positive over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the supply index (INDPRO below 105) indicates weakening business activity, reducing growth expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO stays below 105 for the next month but S&P 500 returns over 20 days are positive (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment (UNRATE above 4.5%) signals labor market weakness, reducing consumer confidence and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises above 4.5% in the next month but S&P 500 returns remain negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising demand (GDPC1) coupled with falling supply (INDPRO) creates a demand-squeeze effect, driving up stock prices and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 increases and INDPRO decreases (as expected), but S&P 500 returns over 20 days are not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.5% intensifies easing, boosting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, FEDFUNDS decline below 2.5% but S&P 500 returns over 20 days are not positive (p > 0.05).
